Prompt engineering, measured on Claude

The model is the same. The words are the lever.

Two prompts for the same customer complaint, sent to the same model, with nothing else in the context. One is what most people type. The other names the goal, the facts, the limits, and the shape. Read both replies and decide which one you would send.

Real outputs from the experiment, unedited. Twelve tasks, ten phrasings each, three Claude models, scored blind. See the numbers.

Results

What we found

Each task was written in ten patterns that hold the job fixed and change only the wording, then run as a fresh subagent on Fable 5.1, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5. A separate judge scored every output blind on correctness, completeness, adherence, usefulness, and concision.

    How to read this

    One run per cell means single-task numbers are noisy; read the pattern and domain averages, not one task. The judge is a Claude model scoring Claude outputs, so absolute scores are less trustworthy than the ordering. Objective checks (exact answers, JSON validity, word limits) back the ordering where the task allowed them. Human ratings from the rating page are collected separately and never mixed into these charts.

    Reference

    Pattern library

    Thirteen patterns, each with the phrasing that works, when it helps, when it hurts, and how strong the evidence is. Strength combines published studies, Anthropic's current guidance, and our runs.

    Ration or avoid

    Tips, threats, and emotional appeals: no reliable gain on 2025 models and high per-question variance. ALL CAPS, "CRITICAL", stacked "always" and "never": current Claude models over-trigger on them, and emphasis spent everywhere is emphasis spent nowhere. Contradictory rules: the top failure mode named by both Anthropic and OpenAI. Politeness or rudeness as a lever: the sign flips between models and years.

    Tool

    Grade a prompt

    Paste a draft. The page scores it against the seven-dimension rubric the skill uses, then asks Claude for the full treatment: scorecard with evidence, the questions worth asking, and three rewrites.

    0

    The quick score looks for surface signals only (a named deliverable, numbers and file names, limits, a format, a check). It cannot know whether your facts are the right ones. Claude can.

    Your turn

    Rate outputs blind

    Two outputs for the same task from the same model. One came from a bare prompt, one from the full-stack prompt. Which one would you use? Your vote is stored with everyone else's and reported next to the judge's scores.

    Claude Code
    
  
    The /prompt-engineer skill
    
  
    
    
    The skill runs the same workflow inside Claude Code, where it can read the project. It collects context from CLAUDE.md, the README, manifests, recent commits, and any file your draft names. It grades the draft out of 100, asks three to six questions in one batch (skipping any the repo already answers), and gives three rewrites with the patterns named and a section on what would push the score higher.
    
    
      
      
    1. Install. Clone the repo and link the skill into your user skills folder:
      2. 
    
    
    
    git clone https://github.com/jiaqi01pd2027-dotcom/Prompt-Engineer.git
ln -s "$(pwd)/Prompt-Engineer/skill/prompt-engineer" ~/.claude/skills/prompt-engineer
    
    
      
      
    1. Use. In any Claude Code session: /prompt-engineer fix the login bug, or paste a prompt and say "grade this". It also triggers when you ask "how should I ask for X".
      2. 
      
    2. Pick a rewrite. A is minimal, B is structured with your project's facts, C is the interview or agentic form. The skill says which it recommends and why.

    What a reply looks like
    
    
    Scorecard: 22/100 (a command, not a prompt)
  Goal and deliverable   4/20  "fix the login bug": which bug, done how?
  Context                2/20  no file, no repro, no issue named
  Constraints            0/15
  Output format          2/15
  Role and audience      0/10  (no meaningful persona here)
  Verification           0/10  no test or check named
  Scope                  4/10  one ask, hidden sub-steps

Context found: Next.js, `npm test`, CLAUDE.md forbids edits under generated/,
last 3 commits touch lib/auth/session.ts, open issue "cookie not cleared on logout".

Rewrite B (recommended):
  Fix the logout bug from the open issue "Session cookie not cleared on logout".
  Start in lib/auth/session.ts. Reproduce it with a failing test in
  lib/auth/__tests__/ matching session.test.ts, then fix the code, not the test.
  Do not edit anything under generated/. Run `npm test` and `npm run lint` and
  paste the results. If the fix needs changes outside lib/auth, stop and tell me.

Patterns applied: specific deliverable, project substitution, few-shot by
pointing at an existing test, verification with a stop rule. Not applied:
role, chain-of-thought.
To push it higher: add the expected behaviour ("after logout, GET /api/me
returns 401") for a projected 90+.
